note: Product rules the system enforces, with the person who decided them. Add a row when a rule changes; mark the old one superseded rather than editing history.

decisions.decision: Until the WordPress migration completes, this application is the directory only and the news site stays on WordPress.
decisions.rationale: The split was taken to protect the marketplace from a premature cutover. It remains the current state; the target state is set by PD-010.

decisions.decision: A lawyer appears in search only when verification_status = 'verified'.
decisions.rationale: The Verified badge has to mean something. A pending profile is a draft; the dashboard tells the lawyer why they are not visible instead of leaving them to guess.

decisions.decision: A law-firm page publishes only when it is complete: name, 120+ character description, location, practice area, email or phone, and one image.
decisions.rationale: A page whose only content is a name cannot rank and cannot convert. Drafts stay editable, invisible in the index, search and sitemap.

decisions.decision: A law firm may be registered by an administrator who is not a lawyer, and a member lawyer is not required to publish.
decisions.rationale: Firm administrators are often practice managers or marketing staff. Requiring a lawyer would exclude legitimate firms; the completeness gate covers the quality risk instead.

decisions.decision: The law-firm plan is ₦1,000,000 per year, flat, including up to 15 lawyer profiles. Lawyers under the plan pay no individual fee.
decisions.rationale: Client instruction: "put N1m per year, we will review it later if necessary. No fees for individual lawyers under the law firm plan." The fee is a firm subscription, not a per-seat price.

decisions.decision: A plan priced above zero but below ₦1,000 is treated as an unset placeholder: shown as "Pricing under review" and not purchasable.
decisions.rationale: The plans table still carries dollar-era figures. Selling a 365-day premium listing for ₦2 is worse than selling nothing, and the guard releases automatically once real naira prices land.

decisions.decision: Advertising stays on the WordPress news site; the directory carries no ad slots.
decisions.rationale: Ad revenue depends on editorial traffic, which remains on WordPress. Ad slot components exist for a future direct-sold offer but are not wired into marketplace pages.

decisions.decision: The directory opens as a founding-listings marketplace, not as a finished one: below 25 verified lawyers the homepage invites listings instead of publishing counts.
decisions.rationale: The alternative is advertising an inventory that does not exist. Honest scarcity recruits suppliers; invented numbers destroy trust once checked.

decisions.decision: An owner may preview their own draft firm page; the public sees a 404.
decisions.rationale: Owners need to see what they are publishing. Leaving drafts publicly addressable would expose thin pages to crawlers and reviewers.

decisions.decision: The target state is off WordPress. The news site migrates gradually, section by section, with WordPress serving anything not yet replaced.
decisions.rationale: A single big-bang cutover carries a media migration, an 11k-URL redirect map, ad re-integration and an untested editorial surface at once. Gradual migration keeps every step reversible and lets one section prove itself before the next moves.

decisions.decision: The news front end is restored and served on non-directory hosts (the *.vercel.app review host), while directory.lawyard.org keeps serving the marketplace. WordPress remains the public news site until its phase completes.
decisions.rationale: The client asked to see the new news website. Serving it by host keeps the directory untouched and avoids a second public, indexable news site.
